title: Laravel 11 is no longer supported
summary: Laravel's support policy states that security fixes for Laravel 11 ended on 2026-03-12; the release no longer receives security or bug fixes from the Laravel project.

constraints: Preserve routes, middleware, authentication, authorization, queues, scheduled jobs, database migrations, and externally visible application behavior while changing the Laravel major.
Upgrade one major at a time and apply each official Laravel upgrade guide in order; do not skip a major when moving to Laravel 13.
Confirm the target Laravel release supports the project's PHP version and align first-party Laravel packages before regenerating composer.lock.

steps.title: Raise the Laravel requirement
steps.instructions: Change laravel/framework from 11.x one major at a time (12 and 13) and update the related first-party package constraints named by each official upgrade guide.

steps.title: Apply each Laravel upgrade guide
steps.instructions: Work through the official upgrade guides for 12 and 13, in order. Review every high-, medium-, and low-impact change that applies to the application and update configuration and code before continuing.

steps.title: Regenerate the Composer lockfile
steps.instructions: Run Composer with dependency updates enabled for laravel/framework and its related packages, review the resolved versions, and keep composer.json and composer.lock together.

verification.purpose: Validate composer.json and composer.lock after updating the framework and related packages.
Confirm the application boots and reports the intended Laravel and PHP versions.
Run the Laravel application test suite on the upgraded framework.
